steps.label: Type the name you want on your notes and tasks
Click Continue
Application Home opens, ready for your first project

notes: Mac first launch is a welcome sheet titled "Welcome to OpenFrame Studio" with the question "What should we call you?" and one field "Your name (required)". Leaving it empty shows "Enter your name." The sheet says: "Your name appears on notes, tasks and project activity. There is no account. It stays on this computer and you can change it any time in Settings." The button is Continue. The captured name is the test name E2E Tester; a public tutorial may show it or blur it. Application Home with no projects says "Create your first project." with the buttons Create Project, Open Existing Project and Restore Backup or Package…, a note "Your work is stored on this Mac" with a Show in Finder link, and the toolbar buttons Global Idea Vault, Settings and the user name. The status line reads "No project open, Offline · Your projects stay on this computer". The team password gate of the internal build was not captured.

reason: Partial: the result screen is the Project Home of the tour's second new project, titled Empty Short, because the tour imported an example script into Night Bus straight after creating it. The step from the New Project sheet to an empty Project Home is real; only the title differs.

steps.label: Click Create Project
Type a title for the film
Click Create
The new project opens on its Project Home

notes: On the Mac the New Project form is a sheet that slides down over Application Home (on Windows it is a dialog). Fields: Title, Type (pop-up with Feature Film and Short Film, screens 013 and 014), Genre, Written by, Location with a Choose… button. Buttons: Cancel and Create; Create stays off until there is a title. With projects already on Application Home the button is called New Project (toolbar), and File > New Project… (Cmd+N on Application Home) also opens the sheet. A new project opens on Project Home with three starting cards: Open Idea Vault, Build Story and Write/Import Screenplay, plus the header line "Feature Film · Created 1 second ago" and the sidebar note "Project stored locally on this Mac". Avoid showing the Empty Short title in the voice-over; say "your new project".

steps.label: Click Home in the sidebar
Click Search, or press Cmd+K
Type a name or a word from the script
Matching scenes and commands appear; pick one to jump there

notes: The project window has a sidebar with the sections Home, Idea Vault, Story, Screenplay, Breakdown, Production, Call Sheets and Files, the project title at the top and "Project stored locally on this Mac" with the save state (Saved) at the bottom. The toolbar holds Hide Sidebar, All Projects, Back and Forward, the Project menu ("Project: Night Bus. Switch or manage projects"), Search, New, Assistant and Settings. Project Home shows QUICK ACCESS (Idea Vault, Beat Board, Screenplay, Production, Call Sheets, Breakdown, Notes & Tasks, Activity, Recently Deleted, Templates), Project Files and RECENT. Search opens the "Search and commands" palette (Cmd+K; esc closes it); empty, it lists commands such as "Go to Story"; typing kiran lists the scenes that mention Kiran. The Mac menu bar also has a Go menu (screen 043: Back, Forward, Home, Idea Vault, Story, Screenplay, Breakdown, Production, Call Sheets, Files, Notes and Tasks, Activity, Recently Deleted, Production Tab, Project Settings, Keyboard Shortcuts) and a File menu (screen 040); menu bar titles are not part of the captured window, so they are not a clickable step here. Help > Keyboard Shortcuts lists every shortcut (screen 053).

Toolbar: Add (menu), Record Note, Quick Capture, Recently Deleted, Undo, Redo, a Which Idea Vault switch (This Project, Global), a View switch (Grid, Card, List, Folder) and Search. The Add menu (screen 248) has Note, Image…, URL…, File…, Audio / Voice Note…, Audio File…, Video…, Quote and Quick Capture. Choosing Note opens an "Untitled note" in the inspector with Title (optional), Note, Research flag, Collections, Pin, Move, Copy to Global Vault, Send to Story and Delete (screen 249). URL… opens Add URL with a link and an optional note (screens 250, 257). The Quick Capture sheet says "Saving to Night Bus · Project Idea Vault" and "Return to save · Shift+Return for a new line · Esc to cancel". After saving a notice reads "Saved to the Project Idea Vault" with Undo. The start screen 252 still shows a quote open in the inspector from the previous action; that is the real state. Image… and File… open the macOS Open panel, which was not captured.

steps.label: In the right-click menu of an idea, click Pin
Click Pinned in the Idea Vault sidebar

notes: Right-clicking an idea card gives Open, Rename, Move…, Pin, Add to Collection…, Tag…, Copy to Global Vault, Send to Story, Research flag (Unchecked, Checked, Needs Expert Check, No flag) and Delete. The pinned idea here is "Rain on the depot roof, a single lamp". The Idea Vault sidebar lists Pinned, Recently added, Collections (New Collection) and Folders (New Folder), and Tags once a tag exists. Selecting a card shows a selection bar "1 selected" with Move to Folder, Add to Collection, Tag, Pin, Copy to Global Vault, Delete and Clear selection (screen 270). Tag opens a sheet "Add tags to …" where tags are separated with commas (screens 271, 277); Move to Folder opens "Move to Folder" (screens 266, 282). Delete moves the idea to Recently Deleted with Undo (screen 298).

steps.label: Click Add
Choose Act
Name the act and press Return
Click Add Sequence in the act
Name the sequence and press Return
Click Add scene in the sequence
A new scene card waits for a short description

notes: Story has four views in a segmented control: Beat Board, Outline, Characters and Timeline. The empty Beat Board reads "Your Beat Board is empty." and "How does my story fit together? Drag cards until the story works.", with Add Scene and Add Act. The toolbar Add menu has Act, Sequence, Beat, Scene Card and From Idea Vault…; other toolbar items: Search / filter cards, Zoom out, Zoom in, Parking Lot (switch), Build Screenplay and More Beat Board actions. Inside an act: Add Scene, Add Sequence, Add Beat; inside a sequence: Add scene. New acts, sequences and cards are named inline in the board, not in a sheet. The Parking Lot at the side holds cards kept out of the story ("Add Beat to the Parking Lot", "Add Scene to the Parking Lot"). Cmd+N makes a new scene card. The board shows no scene numbers ("No scene numbers; they come from the screenplay"). Build Screenplay turns cards into screenplay scenes (screen 220).

steps.label: In Story, click Characters
Click Add Character
Type a name, and if you like a role and a short description
Click Create Character
The character page lists every scene the character appears in

notes: Characters is a view of Story. Empty it says "No characters yet." and "Create your first character. Name is all you need. Role, image and notes are optional." The New Character sheet has Name, Role / title, Image (Choose image…), Short description, Cancel and Create Character. In the capture the role "A ticket inspector on the night route" and the description "Knows every regular by name" were typed too, so screen 232 shows all three fields filled. After creating, a notice "Added character Kiran" offers Undo, and the character page (KIRAN) shows Edit, Open Relationship Map, More actions, "Scenes this character appears in" (found from the screenplay), Relationships (Add Relationship), "Linked Scene Cards (reference only)" with a Link button, and Notes. Typing a name close to an existing one warns about a possible match (screen 234).

steps.text:
INT. BUS DEPOT - NIGHT

notes: The screenplay page has a bottom bar with the Element menu, Hide Scenes, Find and Replace, the Draft menu ("Draft: Draft 1. Switch draft"), Zoom Out, Zoom 100% and Zoom In; the top bar has the Screenplay menu ("Screenplay: Empty Short. Switch screenplay"), Compare, Comments (0) and Screenplay Tools. The Element menu lists Scene Heading, Action, Character, Parenthetical, Dialogue, Transition, Shot, General note (not printed) and Insert Page Break. Mac shortcuts from the app: Cmd+1 Scene Heading, Cmd+2 Action, Cmd+3 Character, Cmd+4 Parenthetical, Cmd+5 Dialogue, Cmd+6 Transition, Cmd+7 Shot, Cmd+Return page break. Tab moves to the next element type and Shift+Tab back; Return at the end of a line starts the element that normally follows (after a character name, dialogue); Return on an empty action line turns it into a scene heading. While typing a heading the editor suggests INT., EXT., INT./EXT. and I/E. The scene list on the left is headed "Scenes (1)". Step 4's text is the whole field after the step; "IN" was already typed in step 3.

The inspector opens on the Comments tab with the quote (here "hand in a kite", labelled "Scene 1 · text comment"), a Comment field, Cancel and Comment. With nothing selected Add Comment makes a scene comment ("Scene 10 · scene comment", screens 070 and 085). The Comments panel has Open and Resolved tabs, Add Comment and Comment on Draft; each comment shows the author, the quote, a link back to the script, Comment actions, Reply and Resolve. The toolbar button counts comments: Comments (1). Comments can be marked In Discussion (screen 133) and resolved (screens 130, 131). Export says "Private notes excluded."

Choose New Draft…
Name the draft

Both drafts side by side, with every change listed

notes: The Draft menu ("Draft: Example-Short (imported). Switch draft") lists the drafts, New Draft…, Manage Drafts… and Renumber Scenes. The New Draft sheet has Draft name, Note (optional), Cancel and Create Draft, and says the source draft stays exactly as it is. After creating, the line "Created draft “Rewrite A”" appears and the Draft menu shows Rewrite A. Compare shows Before and After pop-ups, a Comparison view switch (Text-only, Scene-only, Text inline), Previous change, Next change and Done, a Changes list ("1 line changed in Scene 1", "1 line changed in Scene 8", "8 scenes unchanged") and a summary line. Screenplay Tools > Drafts… opens the Drafts sheet with each draft's Actions (screens 139 to 144). Revisions: after locking, Screenplay Tools > Revisions… opens Revisions with Start Revision; a revision has a Label, a Colour (Blue, Pink, Yellow, Green), a Revision date and an optional Reason (screens 153 to 155), and Page View can show revision marks (screens 158, 159).

steps.label: Click Screenplay Tools
Choose Lock as Shooting Draft…
Check the details and click Lock as Shooting Draft
The draft is locked as the Shooting Draft

notes: The confirmation sheet asks "Lock this draft as the Shooting Draft?" and lists Draft name, Current version, Unresolved review notes, Number of scenes and Last modified, with Cancel and Lock as Shooting Draft. It says locking is a safety state, not a destructive action. The result line reads "Locked “Example-Short (imported)” as the Shooting Draft". From then on Screenplay Tools offers Revisions… instead of Lock as Shooting Draft… (app source; the captured menu on screen 152 still shows the old label, so do not use that screen). Revisions explains that only the project owner can unlock a shooting draft and offers Start Revision (screens 153 to 155).

After it: "Started Revision A. Example-Short (imported) stays locked.", the Draft menu shows Revision A, and Revisions lists "Revision A · Pink" with "Changed scenes in Revision A" and changed pages.
